value.author: pi-ops-292
value.text:
Root cause (issue #292): prepare renders the pending version's heading with --date-from-version, so a resumed candidate (version day before today) is stamped with its version day. The release step then tags it today; pm-changelog by design derives a tagged window's heading from the tag commit date (pm-changelog#120), so post-tag regeneration on unchanged main renders a different day and changelog:check is red on main. The release PR's own CI passes (candidate still untagged), so the failure only appears after the merge.

Design: use the generator's existing --date-fallback flag (applies only while no release tag exists; ignored once the tag exists, so it matches post-tag invocations byte-for-byte). decideDailyRelease now outputs heading_date: today in RELEASE_TIMEZONE, padded ISO, when the version's calendar day is before today; empty for a same-day release, which is therefore unchanged. The 'Generate changelog and release notes' step, in the same in-place package.json policy rewrite that already appends --include-empty, swaps --date-from-version for --date-fallback <heading_date> in the three changelog scripts when resumed, refreshes a stale pin when a candidate is re-prepared on a later day, and restores --date-from-version when the pending version is current again. The release commit carries the pinned spelling, so the release PR's CI (untagged candidate), prepare's nested release:check and post-tag checks on main all regenerate the same bytes with no follow-up regeneration. The date verifier accepts a pinned --date-fallback day (explicit ISO day only) as an equally clock-free alternative to --date-from-version. Rust/justfile releases (CHANGELOG_DATE derived from the tag name) keep their own spelling and are not touched.
